newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher on foreign funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher on foreign funds support.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended firmer on Wednesday as selective blue-chip buying by foreign institutions pushed the key index higher.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended the day 7.96 points higher to 1,234.83, while the all-share EMAS index was up 1.22 to 361.75.

"We have had orders from two different foreign houses over the last few days. There's been some blue-chip buying, but it has been selective," said Ralph Dixon of the International Division of T.A. Securities.
"Regionally, Malaysia still stands quite strong, and is attractive for its liquidity," said Dixon.
Blue-chips like Tenaga, Telekom and Maybank all ended in positive territory, rising between 10 and 30 cents.
United Engineers, whose 1996 full year results are expected to be around double those of 1995 ended the day 40 cents higher at 23 ringgit.
Malaysia's formal acceptance of Singapore's apology for recent adverse comments made by it of Malaysia's Johor state, did not influence share prices on Wednesday, dealers said.
